designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Strong, clean one-ink idea: the stamp is tilted while the tower stays plumb, and the denomination '3.97°' is the real lean angle, which is a quiet, smart joke. The spaced serif caps 'PISA' are well chosen and the tower drawing is crisp, with line weights that will print. But the conceit flips at a distance: on the tee the tower reads as straight and the whole print just looks crooked/misregistered, since the tower is the only true vertical on the shirt. The tower is a narrow column with large dead sky on both sides, so the frame feels underfilled. The flat base sits on a sloped ground line, so it meets the ground at an awkward wedge. The perforation is a loose scallop that ends in blunt square nubs at the corners instead of resolving into proper corner holes. The '3.97°' is small and drifts off-axis from the PISA baseline. At this placement size the stamp reads as a small sticker on the back.
designs.fix: Make the lean read as the tower's, not the print's: square the stamp to the shirt and lean the tower about 4° inside it, anchored to a level ground line, then widen the tower or crop it tighter so it fills the frame, with the perforations redrawn to resolve cleanly at the corners.
